## Goal

One-off operational sweep of the stale `<id>.pending-screens.json` signals left behind by the broken in-main-slot resume cycle fixed in SA-0MVSTZ71J001P67S, so the affected items stop being constrained by a gate that can no longer clear.

Discovered-from: SA-0MVSTZ71J001P67S (audit comment 2026-10-29, "Adjacent scope note 2"). Becomes actionable once the D1/D2 resume fixes land.

## Known backlog (as recorded on 2026-10-29)

| Item | Children pending | Signal written |
|---|---|---|
| LP-0MU3VDB9U008H8CI | 2 | 2026-10-15 |
| LP-0MVB8F5ZU0079DE9 | 1 | 2026-10-20 |
| LP-0MVDVJYN5001BMG4 | 1 | 2026-10-18 |
| LP-0MVGT0E6W000Q8CY | 3 | 2026-10-23 |
| LP-0MVLNBCTN0084MT0 | 2 | 2026-10-29 |
| LP-0MVNTT4X8009IO2X | 3 | 2026-10-29 |
| LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG | 6 | 2026-10-29 |

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Enumerate every `<id>.pending-screens.json` under the `llm` project's `.worklog/audit-checkpoints/` and reconcile the list against the table above (record additions/removals in a comment).
- AC2: For each remaining signal, run the parent audit once with the fix in place; where the child audits are already serviced the signal is cleared automatically, otherwise run a forced `--no-child-in-main-slot` audit so the child screens are executed by the runner instead of being emitted for an absent interactive session.
- AC3: Each affected item's audit state is recorded (report verdict + whether the signal is gone); no signal remains for an item whose children are all audited.
- AC4: The sweep does not change verdicts by hand — `wl audit-set` is never used directly; only real runner audits persist reports.

## Minimal implementation

- Shell loop over the checkpoint dir listing, then per item `python3 skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py issue <id> --no-child-in-main-slot --force` (or the default mode where a fresh serviced child audit exists).
- Collect evidence (log paths + `wl audit-show <id> --json`) into a comment on this item.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (read-only — `--force`, `--no-child-in-main-slot`, `_read_pending_screens_signal`/`_write_pending_screens_signal`)
- `<llm-project>/.worklog/audit-checkpoints/*.pending-screens.json` (the sweep target)

## Dependencies

- Blocked by SA-0MVSTZ71J001P67S (the resume fixes must land first).

## Deliverables

- Empty/cleared signal backlog with per-item evidence recorded.
data.title: Sweep stale in-main-slot pending-screens signals

## Migrated from AH-0MWFHLDAS008YG0P (AI_Hell worklog)

This work was originally tracked in the AI_Hell worklog as
AH-0MWFHLDAS008YG0P and was planned there with two children (Test + Fix).
**The fix lands in this repository** (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`),
so the work is recorded and tracked here (SorraAgents). Original tracking,
comments, evidence and session history live on the AH item and are preserved
there; the description and ACs are mirrored below.

discovered-from:AH-0MWFHLDAS008YG0P

## Problem

When `implement.py drive` spawns a child session that dies before writing
anything (e.g. a transient provider error — `Provider finish_reason: error`),
the child is left `in-progress` with an empty worktree (0 dirty files, 0
commits ahead of dev). The next `drive`/`parent` run then calls
`_child_main_checkout_violation()` for that child, which finds
`_git_path_has_changes(wt)` false (correctly — no work) and therefore
attributes **pre-existing dirt in the main checkout and in other items'
sibling worktrees** to the failed child. The run fails closed with a long
'produced changes in the sibling worktree …' message naming paths the child
never touched.

## Impact during AH-0MWDC3L9I008INDP

Recovering child AH-0MWEXI5460080WEI required a manual `implement.py abort`
before the drive would proceed; the guard's message blamed
`src/test/playSceneBootGuard.test.ts` (main checkout) and files in
`wl-AH-0MTVYBL2L0085G6G`, `wl-AH-0MVAUU594007S92Q`,
`wl-AH-0MWCOWTOR00994NA` and `/tmp/hw-base-check` — all other sessions' work.

## Acceptance criteria

- A driven child left `in-progress` by a **spawn failure** (no changes in its
  worktree, no commits ahead) is treated as startable-again/reset, not as a
  placement violation, so the next `drive` re-spawns it without manual
  `abort`.
- The placement guard distinguishes 'this child wrote elsewhere' from 'this
  child wrote nothing and other surfaces happen to be dirty' — the latter must
  not fail the chain.
- Regression test: a spawn-failed child plus a dirty main checkout and a dirty
  sibling worktree does not produce a `_child_main_checkout_violation`; a
  child that genuinely wrote only into a sibling worktree still does.
- No weakening of the genuine cross-worktree-write detection
  (SA-0MW5FIJNQ002Z24I).

## Key files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_child_main_checkout_violation`
  call sites in `phase_parent` (two sites: `skip-in-progress` path ~15158 and
  `implement` path ~15218)
- `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_sibling_worktree_stray.py` — existing
  sibling stray tests; add the spawn-fail regression

## Related

- SA-0MW5FIJNQ002Z24I — genuine cross-worktree-write detection; must not be
  weakened
- SA-0MVRN5Q67005H3M5 — behind-only child worktree mis-detected as 'has
  changes' and auto-finished (related verdict logic)
- AH-0MWFHLDAS008YG0P — original AI_Hell tracking item

## Plan (plan skill session on AH-0MWFHLDAS008YG0P)

Two children, implemented in dependency order (test-first):

1. **Test** — regression tests for spawn-failed child + dirty main/sibling
   not being a placement violation (6 ACs covering all four parent ACs).
2. **Fix** — code fix in `phase_parent`: check `worktree_verdict` before
   calling `_child_main_checkout_violation()`. Two call sites updated:
   `skip-in-progress` path (~15158) and `implement` path (~15218).

Dependency: Fix depends on Test (test-first ordering).

> Note: on 2026-11-14 the implementation could not be started because a Code
> Freeze was active (SorraAgents ship release in progress, run-release.js pid
> 2707644); the refusal was recorded as a comment on AH-0MWFHLDAS008YG0P.

## Impact

Driving an epic survives a child session that dies before it writes anything: the chain reports the child startable again and continues on the next run instead of stopping on unrelated dirt.
data.title: implement.py drive: spawn-failed child trips the worktree-placement guard on unrelated dirt

## Migrated from AH-0MWGSW7TM003DXBZ (AI_Hell worklog)

Test child of SA-0MWGZ86MS005OE61 (implement.py drive: spawn-failed child
trips the worktree-placement guard). Originally tracked as
AH-0MWGSW7TM003DXBZ.

discovered-from:AH-0MWFHLDAS008YG0P

## Problem

When a driven child spawns but dies before writing anything (spawn-failed),
its worktree exists but is clean (`has_changes=False`,
`worktree_verdict=CHILD_CLEAN`). The next `phase_parent`/`drive` run then
calls `_child_main_checkout_violation()` which scans the main checkout and
sibling worktrees. If those surfaces are dirty (unrelated to the
spawn-failed child), the violation fires incorrectly, blaming the spawn-failed
child for dirt it never produced.

## User Story

As a driver running `implement.py drive` on an epic, I want spawn-failed
children to be resettable without the placement guard incorrectly blaming
them for unrelated dirt in the main checkout or sibling worktrees.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A spawn-failed child (worktree exists, no changes, no commits ahead) is
  treated as startable-again/reset, not as a placement violation, so the next
  `drive` re-spawns it without requiring manual `abort`.
- The placement guard distinguishes 'this child wrote elsewhere' from 'this
  child wrote nothing and other surfaces happen to be dirty' — the latter must
  not fail the chain.
- Regression test: a spawn-failed child plus a dirty main checkout and a dirty
  sibling worktree does not produce a `_child_main_checkout_violation`; a
  child that genuinely wrote only into a sibling worktree still does.
- No weakening of the genuine cross-worktree-write detection
  (SA-0MW5FIJNQ002Z24I) — existing tests in
  `test_drive_sibling_worktree_stray.py` must continue to pass.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_child_main_checkout_violation`
  call sites in `phase_parent`
- `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_sibling_worktree_stray.py` — existing
  sibling stray tests, add the spawn-fail regression

## Tests

1. Spawn-failed child + dirty main checkout + dirty sibling worktree → no
   violation, drive continues (not blocked)
2. Spawn-failed child + clean surfaces → reported for re-implementation (happy
   path unchanged)
3. Genuine cross-worktree write → violation still detected (existing test must
   pass — no weakening)
4. Both `skip-in-progress` and `implement` call paths in `phase_parent`
   covered by tests

## Impact

A spawn-failed child no longer trips the placement guard on unrelated dirt: the next run reports it startable again and re-spawns it, so recovering needs no manual `implement.py abort`.
data.title: Test: spawn-failed child with dirty main/sibling is not a placement violation

## Migrated from AH-0MWGSXPPS003KGOY (AI_Hell worklog)

Fix child of SA-0MWGZ86MS005OE61 (implement.py drive: spawn-failed child
trips the worktree-placement guard). Originally tracked as
AH-0MWGSXPPS003KGOY.

discovered-from:AH-0MWFHLDAS008YG0P

## Problem

`phase_parent` calls `_child_main_checkout_violation()` whenever a child has a
worktree but `has_changes=False`. This function then scans the main checkout
and sibling worktrees for changes. If unrelated dirt is found (e.g. from a
spawn-failed child that wrote nothing), the violation fires incorrectly.

## Fix

In `phase_parent`, at the two call sites where `_child_main_checkout_violation`
is called (the `skip-in-progress` path and the `implement` path), check
`worktree_verdict` before calling the violation function:

1. If `worktree_verdict == CHILD_NO_WORK`: record as not-finalisable and
   continue (the spawn-failed child wrote nothing — same handling as the
   `has_changes=True, CHILD_NO_WORK` path).
2. If `worktree_verdict == CHILD_CLEAN`: call
   `_child_main_checkout_violation` as before (the child is truly clean,
   foreign dirt is suspicious).
3. For any other verdict with `has_changes=False`: call
   `_child_main_checkout_violation` as before (defensive).

This ensures a spawn-failed child (clean worktree, no changes) with unrelated
foreign dirt is reported for re-implementation rather than blocking the drive
chain.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Spawn-failed children with `CHILD_CLEAN` worktrees are reported for
  re-implementation (not blocked by foreign dirt).
- Spawn-failed children with `CHILD_NO_WORK` worktrees (state-file-only dirt)
  are recorded as not-finalisable.
- The placement guard still detects genuine cross-worktree writes — no
  weakening of SA-0MW5FIJNQ002Z24I.
- Both call sites in `phase_parent` are updated consistently.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_parent` function, two call
  sites for `_child_main_checkout_violation`

**Dependencies:**
- Depends on the Test child (SA-0MWGZ8E7C001X2HA) — tests must be
  implemented first (test-first ordering).

## Impact

Recovering from a child session that dies before writing anything no longer needs a manual `implement.py abort`: the next `drive` re-spawns the child instead of stopping on dirt it never produced.
data.title: Fix: spawn-failed child with no-work worktree should not trigger placement violation
